html:
Mbailundu, or Bailundo, was the largest of the Ovimbundu kingdoms on the central highlands of Angola. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

Its caravans carried rubber, wax and ivory from the interior to the coast at Benguela. When the price of wild rubber fell and Portuguese traders cheated and enslaved local people, Mbailundu rose in 1902, led by the war chief Mutu ya Kevela. Portuguese troops crushed the Bailundo revolt within months, and the kingdom came under direct Portuguese rule. The town of Bailundo stands near its old capital.
